page: Microsoft Azure L16as_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For storage-heavy workloads, it bundles 3840 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core results placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations fall within the average tier. Memory performance shows a clear tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth are average, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is a bottleneck, with 70B model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 10%, though text generation with small 135M models remains strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L16as_v4 offers a dense resource profile, combining high-capacity local storage with a substantial memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective option for workloads that require high local storage capacity without the premium cost of dedicated GPU hardware. It is highly suitable for relational databases, NoSQL data stores, caching layers like Redis, and general-purpose memory-intensive applications.

Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 128.0 GB of RAM and 3840 GB of local storage. Benchmarks reveal strong single-core CPU performance and text processing capabilities, alongside average multi-core execution and database operations. However, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25%. Lacking a GPU, this instance is not designed for heavy AI training but excels at text generation for small models. It is highly suited for database hosting, caching systems, and storage-intensive enterprise workloads requiring a balanced 1:8 memory-to-vCPU ratio.
